leila: Heads-up — added canary canary-kv-longctx-0306 that brings up magnet30b-int4 on dedicated nodes. Quick smoke shows a divergence around token ~12500.
ryan: where does it diverge — generation semantics or exact token shift? :thinking_face:
leila: generation semantics. First ~12k tokens match the float16 baseline, after that we see frequent token skips and the LM starts repeating fragments.
anita: any pattern to the skips? periodic or boundary-aligned?
leila: looks aligned to 4096-stride boundaries. Example: after token 12288 (3 * 4096) the KV indices appear to shift by 1 repeatedly.
samir: that smells like a RoPE anchoring/phase wrap issue during prefill -> inflight merge. Could be index arithmetic when we shrink the kv-window for int4 path.
leila: agreed. Repro snippet I ran locally (minimal):

```
python -m repro.generate \ 
  --model magnet30b-int4 \ 
  --prompt-file tests/long_prompts/nostop_20k.txt \ 
  --quant-path deploy/canaries/magnet30b/int4/ \ 
  --max-tokens 4000 \ 
  --seed 42 
```

leila: logs show repeated message: "kv_index: expected 18432 got 18431 — wrapping correction applied" around the divergence point.
ryan: can you paste a short token diff? one side-by-side from fp16 vs int4
leila: fp16: "...the committee agreed to..."  int4: "...the committee agreed the committee agreed to..."
anita: repetition suggests some keys were re-used or the attention window replayed the same prefix. Could also be a prefill stride rounding bug for int4 where we do integer division for block indexing.
samir: hypothesis: our quantized kernel packs keys into narrower lanes and our kvcache offset computation uses floor-div earlier in the code path — causing an off-by-one at boundaries when (context_len % stride) == 0.
leila: QoL note: this only reproduces with sequence length >= ~12000 and when using packed int4 backend. float32/16 path unaffected.
ryan: what's the eval metric delta? perplexity / exact-match?
leila: quick eval on our rolling goldset (longforms-5k) — fp16 PPL 8.9, int4 PPL 12.4 after the boundary; prior to boundary both ~8.9. BLEU-ish style ngram match drops 6 points.
samir: can we induce a smaller repro that triggers earlier? maybe craft adversarial prefix to align with 4096 boundary quicker.
leila: tried a padded prompt forcing prefill length = 4096*2 exactly, and the issue appears immediately after token 8192. So boundary alignment seems causal.
ryan: good repro. Next steps?
leila: I opened a canary job with extra kvcache validation (canary-kv-longctx-0306-verify) that computes a fingerprint per shard and compares with fp16 reference during prefill+inflight. It fails at the same boundary.
leila: failing fingerprint snippet: "shard 7 fingerprint mismatch: ref=0x3f2a7b, canary=0x3f2a79"
anita: 0x...79 vs 0x...7b — off-by-2 difference in fingerprint. Might indicate a two-element swap or missing token pair.
samir: check where we compress keys for int4. We changed memcpy alignment earlier in the onboard PR — maybe the rounding when packing bits across word boundaries is off by 1 byte on some platforms.
leila: note: this reproduces on p4d and a100-int4 nodes but not on local cpu tests (obviously). ops-bot: any env differences in drivers between those fleets?
ops-bot: a100 nodes on us-west have cudnn 8.6.0, driver 535.86.10. p4d fleet uses driver 535.54.01. No config changes this week.
ryan: unlikely driver but still possible; focus on code paths first. samir, can you add assertions to the int4 pack/unpack that check per-shard lengths and bit offsets?
samir: will do. Also I'll add a debug mode to skip packing and run int4 sequence in non-packed fallback to confirm packing is culprit.
leila: timeline: if we can repro locally with small injected padding and create unit test, we can block the canary and roll back quantized pack change.
leila: also ran small ablation: disabling ROPE scaling correction (scale_to_context) removes the divergence but causes quality drop overall. So there's an interaction between RoPE scaling and packed kvcache offsets.
ryan: interesting. Might be that we apply phase scaling at a different granularity for packed keys. If we multiply by scale then shift, rounding error can alter indexing when we compress.
anita: suggested short fix: ensure kvcache write uses absolute byte offsets (computed in 64-bit) before any quantization, then pack. That would decouple phase math from packing rounding.
samir: implementing that now, will push a debug PR to branch/kv-int4-pack-debug and trigger canary.
leila: thanks. I'm attaching the failing prompt and token-diff output to the canary ticket.
leila: tags: @samir @ryan please monitor canary-kv-longctx-0306-verify. I pinned retention logs to 72h.
ryan: thanks — will watch. If this is confirmed, we should include a postmortem-style note in eng-ml/confluence about packing-edge-cases for longctx onboarding.
leila: agreed. For now, throttling the canary and reverting the pack optimization if PR doesn't land in 6 hours.
dev-ci-bot: CI check started for branch/kv-int4-pack-debug — build queued.
samir: pushed initial assertions. CI green on unit tests that exercise packing offsets. Kicking canary now.
leila: canary reports: fingerprint mismatch gone for the two initial shards, still failing on shards 10..12. digging.
ryan: keep updates here. if you need ops to repro on a specific instance id, ping.
leila: will do. thanks everyone :thumbsup:"
